page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-32 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration built on the x86_64 architecture using Intel processors. The instance provides 32 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, supported by 260 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or dedicated GPU accelerators, requiring reliance on external storage infrastructure for persistent data, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory subsystem performance alongside competent general-purpose computing. The instance achieves top-quartile performance in uncached memory bandwidth tests, recording 208.51 GB/sec for large-block reads and 99.59 GB/sec for writes. Computational tests indicate steady middle-tier results, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 15821.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 38513.51. High instruction throughput is evident in image processing benchmarks and static web serving, where throughput reaches 44.59 GB/sec. The underlying processor also exposes modern instruction extensions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, which aid small-model inference and vectorized routines.

The primary tradeoff of the n4-highmem-32 is its reliance on networked block storage due to the absence of integrated NVMe drives. However, its high memory density relative to core count delivers favorable qualitative resource efficiency for workloads constrained by RAM rather than raw CPU cycles. The instance is suited for memory-intensive tasks such as large-scale Redis deployments, enterprise in-memory databases, batch data transformation pipelines, and high-concurrency web services.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-32 is an x86_64 instance offering 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 Intel physical cores and 256 GB of system memory, yielding an 8 GB per core ratio. Built without bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, this instance relies on network-attached volumes for data retention. Benchmark testing highlights strong uncached memory bandwidth, achieving 208.51 GB/sec read and 99.59 GB/sec write throughput, alongside a high static web serving rate of 44.59 GB/sec. Advanced vector extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX support vectorized arithmetic and accelerated matrix computation. With balanced processing power and high memory allocation per vCPU, the n4-highmem-32 provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound tasks, making it a viable configuration for in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, data engineering pipelines, and memory-heavy web application services.
